Sub-topics:
Meeting 1 — Docker & the shared environment:
• Pre-work: install WSL2 + Docker Desktop (Windows) / Docker Desktop (Mac) — everyone on the same footing
• Why containers: reproducibility and a shared, deterministic environment
• Images & containers: pull, run, exec into a container
• Linux on a container: working inside the shared distro — filesystem & basic CLI
• Volumes & ports: persistence and networking
• Docker Compose: the multi-service reproducible dev environment used all course
Meeting 2 — OS & compute fundamentals:
• The machine model: CPU, RAM, disk, network — and a cost intuition for each
• Memory hierarchy (cache to RAM to disk), caching, and running out: spills & OOM
• CPU & concurrency: cores, parallelism vs concurrency, CPU-bound vs I/O-bound
• Disk & I/O: HDD vs SSD, sequential vs random access, throughput vs latency
• Network: bandwidth vs latency; the network as the slowest link when distributed
• Serialization: crossing memory/disk/network boundaries (foreshadows Parquet/Avro & the shuffle)
• Scaling: vertical limits to horizontal scaling — why distributed systems exist; latency numbers every engineer should know

M1 — Python basics (builds on pre-shared Python & Git kits; class = fast review + live coding & exercises):
• Python as an interpreted language: REPL, no compile step, runtime errors
• Syntax, control flow (conditionals, loops), functions
• Package management with uv & pip; virtual environments
• Type hints, error handling, logging
• Basic debugging: reading tracebacks, breakpoints, using a debugger
• Jupyter notebooks: the concept, and notebook (exploration) vs modules (production)
• Git walk-through (based on the Git kit): workflow, commits, branching, PRs
M2 — Data structures & complexity:
• Core structures in depth: lists, tuples, dicts, sets, stacks, queues, hashing (+ trees conceptually)
• Big O notation: time & space complexity and how to estimate it
• Choosing the right structure for the job
• Comprehensions & generators as the pythonic way to work with them
M3 — Code organization, OOP & interfaces:
• Code organization: modules, packages, separation of concerns
• OOP: classes, composition over inheritance
• Interfaces / protocols / duck typing; intro to SOLID
M4 — Design patterns & data access:
• Common design patterns for DE (factory, strategy, repository, ...)
• ORM (SQLAlchemy) & migrations (Alembic)
• API & webhook clients: auth, pagination, rate limits, retries
M5 — Testing, quality & TDD:
• Unit & integration tests, fixtures, mocking, coverage
• TDD (red-green-refactor); refactoring
• Linters & formatters; CI basics (running tests automatically)
M6 — AI-assisted development & SDD:
• Maintainability-first: cheap generation makes clean code, patterns & tests matter more
• AI tooling & prompting techniques
• Applying clean code / patterns / TDD to AI output and verifying it
• Spec-Driven Development (SDD) with OpenSpec

(Core SQL is a course prerequisite — no class time on SELECT/JOIN/GROUP BY)
M1 — What is a database, in depth (Postgres as the lens):
• What a DB actually is: the problem it solves beyond 'a place to store data'
• Postgres architecture: cooperating processes + shared memory (postmaster, backends, background workers, shared buffers, WAL)
• Disk layout: how data physically lives on disk (pages/heap, WAL)
• The life of a query: parser, planner, executor
M2 — Performance: the optimizer, EXPLAIN & indexes:
• What the query optimizer/planner is and does
• Reading EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE: seq scan vs index scan, joins, costs vs actuals
• Analyzing different queries hands-on
• Indexes as a direct descendant of the Python data-structures lesson: B-trees & hash indexes — what an index is underneath
• When to add an index: cost/benefit, write overhead, how to decide; ANALYZE & statistics
M3 — Transactions, isolation & MVCC:
• Transactions & ACID
• Isolation levels and the anomalies they prevent
• Basic MVCC: row versions, how Postgres implements it
• How MVCC & isolation affect performance: vacuum/bloat, lock contention

M1 — Why a warehouse: OLTP vs OLAP & MPP:
• OLTP vs OLAP: why you can't just run analytics on your production DB
• Dimensional modeling: star/snowflake, facts & dimensions, SCD
• Normalization vs denormalization — and why analytics denormalizes
• MPP concepts: how a warehouse parallelizes a query across nodes — the first real-life distributed-systems material (sets up Spark)
M2 — Storage formats & how MPP works under the hood:
• Row vs columnar storage — why columnar makes OLAP/MPP fast
• Data formats: Parquet, Avro, ORC; compression & encoding
• Partitioning & file layout, leading to parallel scans
• Table formats (Iceberg/Delta) — concept
• Connection to sources and the lake

M1 — Pipelines by hand I (building):
• Build bronze-silver-gold with vanilla Python + Postgres (containerized)
• Extract patterns: full vs incremental
• Load patterns: append, upsert/merge, overwrite
• SCD application
M2 — Pipelines by hand II (operating = primitive Airflow):
• Idempotency (safe re-runs) & incrementality (watermarks)
• Control/manage table: run history, watermarks, status
• Scheduling with cron; mini-DAG dependency walker
• Retries, error handling & failure recovery
• Backfilling & late-arriving data
• Atomic loads: staging tables & swaps (callback to MVCC/transactions)
M3 — Airflow, the real orchestrator:
• DAGs, operators, sensors, hooks, XComs, scheduling, retries, backfills — mapped onto the primitive they built
• Managed Airflow (MWAA) as the cloud variant
• Dagster shown as the modern asset-based alternative
M4 — ELT & dbt I:
• ETL vs ELT: push transformation into the warehouse
• dbt: models, sources, refs, materializations
• Building silver-gold transformations in dbt (hands-on)
M5 — ELT & dbt II:
• dbt tests, lineage & docs
• Snapshots (SCD in dbt); incremental models
• CDC as a concept (Debezium as a brief mention)
• Consolidate the anchor project's pipeline end-to-end

M1 — Cloud foundations (theory):
• Why cloud: rent-vs-own, elasticity, managed services; regions & AZs; shared-responsibility model
• IAM: roles, policies, least privilege
• Networking: VPC, subnets, security groups
• S3 as the data lake; the cost mindset
M2 — Services & IaC (theory):
• Compute & containers: ECS + ECR (run the Docker pipeline images from Module 1); EKS/K8s at a high level only
• Managed DB: RDS
• Lake & analytics: S3, Glue (catalog + ETL), Athena, Redshift (managed warehouse — concept)
• Terraform: IaC as a concept, generated with AI
M3 — Make the project cloud-native (hands-on):
• Source files to S3
• Python ETL containers to ECR (registry) + ECS (run)
• Processed data to S3 (Parquet) + Glue Data Catalog
• Query/serving via Athena
• Orchestration on MWAA (managed Airflow); Airflow on EKS as a big-org mention
• Guided build + AI-generated Terraform (time-boxed)
• Leaves data on S3 + catalog ready, so Spark provisions compute over it next
• [Distributed-systems thread] managed MPP query (Athena/Redshift) — the Spark shuffle, managed

M1 — Build primitive Spark (live, step by step in class — no skeleton):
• Build a toy distributed processor together, adding a piece per concept
• Partitioning the data
• Parallel map across workers (coordinator/worker model)
• Shuffle: moving data between stages
• Reduce/aggregate; feel why distribution is hard and why a framework helps
M2 — Architecture, tradeoffs & scaling:
• Architecture: driver, executors, cluster manager; jobs, stages, tasks
• RDDs to DataFrames; lazy evaluation & the DAG
• Partitions & parallelism; narrow vs wide transformations
• Scaling: executors/cores, vertical vs horizontal (callback to Module 1)
• Tradeoffs: Spark's overhead vs single-machine Python/pandas — when it pays off
M3 — Distributed mechanics & what can go wrong:
• Shuffle & data movement; spill to disk (callback to Module 1)
• Skew: one partition/key dominating
• Stragglers: a single worker taking most of the work; a weak worker raising latency
• Joins & broadcast (avoiding shuffles); caching/persistence
• Fault tolerance via lineage & recomputation
• Reading the Spark UI to diagnose; partitioning strategies to fix
M4 — Rewriting vanilla Python to Spark on EMR (hands-on):
• Migrate the project's transforms from vanilla Python to PySpark
• Blow up the data volume on the same schema: vanilla Python crashes, Spark to the rescue
• Run on a real EMR cluster reading S3 + Glue Data Catalog (from the cloud module)
• Measure the speedup; Spark SQL
• When Spark wins vs when it doesn't; batch vs Structured Streaming (intro, bridges to Kafka)
• [Distributed-systems thread] PRIMARY hands-on lab

M1 — Why streaming & Kafka fundamentals (the distributed log):
• Batch vs streaming: when you actually need real-time
• Kafka's append-only log model; light in-class demo — a tiny append-only log to feel offsets & consumer position
• Architecture: brokers, topics, partitions, offsets
• Producers & consumers; consumer groups & rebalancing
• Replication, leader election & ISR — kill-a-broker demo
M2 — Practical streaming, hands-on (enhance the project with a streaming source):
• Delivery semantics in practice: at-least-once / exactly-once; idempotent consumers (callback to pipeline idempotency)
• Practical design: partitioning for throughput, consumer scaling, offset management & commits
• Hands-on: add a new streaming source to the anchor project — Kafka producer to Spark Structured Streaming to the lake
• Batch vs streaming decisions revisited
• [Distributed-systems thread] replication & delivery semantics anchor

(1 meeting — concept-first, using the dbt tooling they already know)
• Why data quality: the cost of bad data; quality dimensions (completeness, accuracy, freshness, uniqueness, validity, consistency)
• dbt tests: built-in (not_null, unique, accepted_values, relationships) + singular tests
• dbt-expectations package: richer expectations (ranges, sets, distributions, row counts)
• Schema drift; freshness, volume & anomaly checks
• Quality gates between bronze/silver/gold — hands-on on the anchor project
• Data contracts & SLAs (concept)

(1 meeting — observability-heavy; concept + hands-on)
• The DataOps mindset: pipelines as production software
• Operational observability: metrics, logs, traces — Prometheus + Grafana; CloudWatch for the cloud pipeline
• Monitoring pipeline health: run durations, failure rates, freshness as an operational SLA (vs Module 9's data-correctness view)
• Hands-on: build a Grafana dashboard + an alert on the anchor pipeline
• Alerting & on-call basics
• CI/CD for data pipelines: consolidation recap (CI from Module 2 + cloud deploy from the cloud module) into the production release picture

M1 — NoSQL concepts & key-value stores:
• Why & when NoSQL; the family landscape and what each type gives you (key-value, document, wide-column, graph, search)
• Key-value stores: what they give you (low-latency, caching, simple model)
• Access patterns & data modeling for key-value
• Hands-on: connect to Redis; core operations (strings, hashes, TTL, caching pattern)
M2 — Document stores:
• Document model: what it gives you (flexible/nested schema, developer ergonomics)
• Access patterns & data modeling: embedding vs referencing, design around queries
• Hands-on: connect to MongoDB; CRUD, queries, aggregation basics
• [Distributed-systems thread] consistency models (eventual consistency, quorum) woven through both

M1 — Agents development (tool-agnostic):
• LLM APIs & tool use
• RAG & vector databases as the agent's plumbing
• Prompt engineering
• Building a working agent
• Hands-on: an agent over the project's data (natural-language question to warehouse query)
M2 — DS pipelines & basic MLOps:
• The DE's role around ML: feature pipelines, training/serving data flows
• Model & artifact versioning; batch vs online inference
• Monitoring data & model drift
• Hands-on: a feature pipeline off the gold layer + serve a simple model

Final meeting — presentations, defense & interview readiness (everything comes together):
• Present & defend the end-to-end project
• System-design review: explain the architecture and justify the tradeoffs
• Mock interviews: common DE interview questions; telling the pipeline story end-to-end
• Final readiness check: can they pass a real-life DE interview?
